solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: World traveller

parts.note: a globe is the world
a trotter is one who trots, a traveller on foot

explanation.surface: Someone who has travelled all over the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who travels widely across many countries is commonly called this.

clue.text: Grain initially sold in ounces — one doesn't buy much in Warsaw

definitions.text: one doesn't buy much in Warsaw

parts.note: GR is the standard abbreviation for grain, the small unit of weight

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the abbreviation for ounces

parts.note: OZ is the abbreviation for ounces

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word sold

explanation.surface: A grocer weighing out grain in ounces, with a joke about tiny Polish money.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small Polish coin, a hundredth of a zloty, so it buys very little in Poland's capital.

clue.text: Women in the pub attractive to slimmers

indicators.note: in places the women abbreviation inside the word for the pub

parts.note: the local is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: Women at the local bar appealing to people on a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is low in calories, in the informal shortened form, appeals to dieters.

clue.text: Financier making name in Mumbai, one abandoned by mother initially

indicators.note: in signals the name abbreviation being placed inside what remains
abandoned by signals that the word for mother is dropped from the Indian city plus the letter for one
initially says the dropped word for mother sits at the start

parts.note: mum is an everyday word for mother
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A banker making a name for himself in India's commercial capital, who was abandoned by his mother early on.
explanation.walkthrough: MUMBAI plus A, with MUM dropped from the front, leaves BAIA; 'making ... in' puts N into it.
explanation.definitionFit: In India, a member of the trading and money-lending caste, hence a merchant or financier.

clue.text: Colour round aitu fashioned in rock

indicators.note: round says the colour word is wrapped about the rearranged letters

parts.note: a tinge is a slight colour or tint

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters of aitu are rearranged

explanation.surface: Colour worked around a Polynesian demigod's figure carved in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: An aitu is a Polynesian demigod; 'fashioned' rearranges its letters and 'round' sets the colour word about them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kind of igneous rock, a variety of phonolite named after a Norwegian locality.

clue.text: Legendary bird giving scoundrel a lift

indicators.note: giving pairs with a lift to describe raising the word for scoundrel in this down clue
a lift in a down clue means the word for scoundrel is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A mythical bird kindly carrying a villain into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of roc, the giant bird of Arabian tales such as Sinbad's voyages.

clue.text: I'm getting added energy in every Parisian break (7, two words)

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the French word

parts.note: tout is French for every or all, French being the language of Paris
taken as written without the apostrophe
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of extra vigour during every break taken in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause in play called by a team or official, a short break from activity.

clue.text: Test when attached to end of rope, part of mountaineer's kit

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of the word rope

parts.note: Chambers gives a word for one who tries that also means a test or trial

explanation.surface: Testing a climbing aid tied to the rope's end.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short rope ladder with a few rungs, used by climbers as a foothold in artificial climbing.

clue.text: Take ill? Doctor enters

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of enters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone falls sick and the doctor walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take ill' reads as falling sick, but it means take amiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something ill is to be offended by it, which is to feel aggrieved about it.

clue.text: Lilting airs filling old space in special garden

indicators.note: filling says the rearranged letters go inside the old word for space

parts.note: roum is an old spelling of room, meaning space

indicators.note: lilting means sung with a swinging rhythm, so the letters of airs are moved about

explanation.surface: Lilting tunes fill an old space in a particular garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lilting' rearranges airs into the Indian garment, which 'filling' puts inside the old word for room.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosarium is a rose garden, a garden given over to one flower.

clue.text: Creeping mare's poorly, bit of tackle stuck in muzzle?

indicators.note: poorly means unwell, out of shape, so the letters of mare's are rearranged
stuck in places the picked letter inside the word for muzzle

parts.note: a muzzle is an animal's nose and mouth, hence nose

indicators.note: bit of asks for just the first letter of tackle

explanation.surface: A sick horse with a piece of harness lodged in its snout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges the five letters of mare's; 'stuck in' lodges the T inside the muzzle word.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany this describes a plant producing runners, so creeping along the ground.

clue.text: Love in boarding house curtailed, making one glum

indicators.note: in places the love god inside the shortened word
curtailed means cut short, so the boarding house word loses its last letter

parts.note: a pension is a continental boarding house
Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: Romance in a cheap lodging house cut short, leaving someone gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for a thoughtful, melancholy person, as in Milton's Il Penseroso, so a brooding person.

clue.text: Son mixed up with crime? Such types are new to the area

definitions.text: Such types are new to the area

indicators.note: mixed up with means jumbled together, so son and crime are rearranged as one

explanation.surface: A young man drawn into crime, blamed on newcomers to the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have recently moved into a district are newcomers to it.

clue.text: Old buck: in other words a disreputable fellow

parts.note: sc is short for scilicet, Latin for namely, in other words
a rip is a dissolute, worthless person

explanation.surface: An old dandy, in other words a bit of a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old buck' suggests a dashing old man, but buck is slang for a dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrip was paper currency issued in place of money, a buck being slang for a dollar.

clue.text: Environmentalist down under that is behind grand waterway

indicators.note: behind says the that-is abbreviation comes after the other pieces

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
a reen is a drainage ditch or watercourse in south-west England
IE is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: An Australian conservationist standing behind a great canal.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a conservationist, someone campaigning on green issues.

clue.text: Beans a success? Seconds called for

parts.note: runners are runner beans, a climbing variety
up can mean successful or ahead, as in a venture being up

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether the bean crop thrived and calls for second helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: Those placed second in a contest are the runners-up.

clue.text: Rain tree from South Africa? I am surprised

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
man! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone astonished to hear a tree comes from South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The rain tree, a tropical American tree of the pea family, is also known by this name.

clue.text: Old-style footwear shone when reconditioned

indicators.note: reconditioned means rebuilt, so the letters of shone are reassembled

explanation.surface: Old boots that gleamed after being restored.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosen is the archaic plural of hose, meaning stockings or leggings.

clue.text: Chump trailing behind people missing 50%? Common in Shakespeare

indicators.note: trailing behind says the head word follows the shortened people
missing 50% means half the six letters of people are lost

parts.note: chump is slang for the head, as is bean

explanation.surface: A fool lagging behind half-absent people, written in old English.
explanation.walkthrough: PEOPLE loses its middle three letters, EOP, for PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's spelling of plebeian, meaning belonging to the common people.

clue.text: Sakia activated in big but not grand Indian festival

indicators.note: in places the stirred letters inside what is left
but not means the big word lacks the grand letter

parts.note: G is slang for a grand

indicators.note: activated means set in motion, so the letters of Sakia are stirred

explanation.surface: An Indian water wheel set working at a large festival.
explanation.walkthrough: A sakia is an Indian water wheel; 'activated' turns it into AISAK, placed in BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Baisakhi, here spelt thus, is the Sikh and Hindu new-year harvest festival.

clue.text: What'll provide lashings first put away in jet?

indicators.note: first put away means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a squirt is a thin jet of liquid

explanation.surface: A riddle about what is first tucked into a jet of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A quirt is a short riding whip with a braided lash, used for whipping.

clue.text: Part of chronicles, one read both ways, Latin

indicators.note: read both ways means the girl's name is the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name, one person

explanation.surface: Part of a history book, read forwards and backwards, written in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a single year's record, the singular of annals, chronicles.

clue.text: Highlight a double-headed coin

indicators.note: double-headed means the coin's first letter appears twice

parts.note: a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A trick coin with heads on both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To accent something is to stress it, to emphasise it.

clue.text: Reruns given a pasting, making one tender

indicators.note: given a pasting means beaten up, so the letters of reruns are rearranged

explanation.surface: Repeat programmes savaged by critics, which leaves one feeling sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' reads as sore, but here it is a noun: one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurser is someone who nurses or looks after another, a carer.

clue.text: Arches, among the characteristics of Greece?

parts.note: in means among
greece is an archaic word for a flight of steps, so steps are what it consists of

explanation.surface: Architectural arches, a hallmark of classical Greek buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: Greece suggests the country, but Chambers lists greece (also grece) as an old word for a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the arched upper part of the foot.

clue.text: What's downy after start of pogonotomy I fail to keep

indicators.note: start of asks for the first letter of pogonotomy

parts.note: to lose something is to fail to keep it

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps their fuzz after their first attempt at shaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Pogonotomy is a rare word for shaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilose means hairy, covered with fine soft hair.

clue.text: Waxy stuff to take over on the floor?

definitions.meaning: a waxy substance forming the cuticle on plant leaves

definitions.text: to take over on the floor?
definitions.meaning: to interrupt a dancing couple and take one partner's place

explanation.definitionFit: Plant cuticle wax has this name, and the phrase also means interrupting dancers to replace a partner.

clue.text: Lands of poesy wherein Caffir roams (not very strong)

indicators.note: roams means wanders about, so the remaining letters are scattered
not very turns very strong, the double forte in the word, into single strength by losing one

parts.note: F stands for forte, strong, in music

explanation.surface: A poem's African landscape over which a tribesman wanders, not especially powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: CAFFIR has FF, fortissimo; 'not very' drops one F, and 'roams' rearranges CAFIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Afric is a poetic name for Africa, the continent.

clue.text: Spring, time to follow love in frivolity

indicators.note: to follow says the time abbreviation comes last
in places the love letter inside the fun word

parts.note: frivolity is light-hearted fun
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Some time spent having fun after a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fount is a spring or source of water, a fountain.

clue.text: One heading left or right, we hear, for strong drink (beware second!)

indicators.note: we hear signals that the result sounds like the earlier phrase

parts.note: a sider would be one who heads off to the side, left or right

explanation.surface: A footballer directing a header sideways, then warned off the strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: '(beware second!)' warns that the second letter is Y, the old spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyder is an archaic spelling of cider, an alcoholic apple drink.

clue.text: One on a zebra, not so good-tempered?

definitions.meaning: a zebra is a British zebra crossing, so one using it is crossing the road

explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian traversing a zebra crossing, and also the comparative of cross, meaning angrier.

clue.text: Attend college, not top — Little Rock

parts.note: to go to something is to attend it

indicators.note: not top means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a poly is a polytechnic college

explanation.surface: Going to college without reaching the top, in an Arkansas city.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Rock looks like the American city, but is a small stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gooly is Australian slang for a stone or pebble.

clue.text: Lamb maybe sits easy in a stew

indicators.note: in a stew means agitated, so the letters of sits easy are churned

explanation.surface: A lamb sits comfortably in a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamb is Charles Lamb, the essayist known as Elia, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb is a famous example of a writer of essays.

clue.text: Governing party? Pity when leader takes a tumble

indicators.note: the first letter falls to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: a sin is something regrettable, as in it is a sin, a pity

explanation.surface: It is a shame when the party head falls from power.
explanation.definitionFit: The ins are those in office, the party currently holding power.

clue.text: Feature of pugs, ones retiring with broken bones (8, two words)

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for ones is read backwards

parts.note: 'uns is dialect for ones

indicators.note: broken means the letters of bones are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Shy dogs with broken bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses UNS to SNU; 'broken' turns BONES into BNOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pugs have a short, upturned nose, a characteristic of the breed.

clue.text: Platform regular practises with craftsman

parts.note: to train is to practise
a potter is a craftsman in clay

explanation.surface: A craftsman who rehearses regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbyist who logs locomotives stands on railway platforms regularly.
